transformNote: the Strait asserted open under US control (the 10-20 Fox object; the night lane under US protection per Lloyd's List, 10-22). lines.quote: European, Middle East ministers urge US-Iran diplomacy, not new attacks
lines.note: THE DOOR: a plea is the frame; the Strait — the meeting's stated subject — is not in the headline. 'Not new attacks' dates the page: the strike is expected
lines.zWhy: ministers urging no new attacks read a strait a strike would close further

lines.quote: foreign ministers of eight countries warn the US against further attacks on Iran after meeting in Türkiye on the Strait of Hormuz and other regional issues
lines.note: THE SUBJECT: the meeting is called on the Strait. Eight governments convening on a lane the US says it controls is the page's lowest-Dia statement of the object
lines.zWhy: a meeting called to discuss the Strait reads it as not settled

lines.quote: the E3 — the UK, France and Germany — met Friday with the R4 — Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Egypt — with Italy attending
lines.note: the instrument: who sat. Two Gulf littoral states, the three European signatories, the host. No US seat at the table
lines.zWhy: a table without the holder reads the holder's control as incomplete

lines.quote: no participating country supported another military intervention or attack on Iran
lines.note: the host's count: zero of eight. A dated statement by the convener
lines.zWhy: eight against a strike is a strait eight expect to be struck near

lines.quote: such a move would increase tensions and widen the conflict; diplomacy and dialogue the only way to end the war
lines.note: 'the only way' is the frame — a verdict on method, not a reading of the lane
lines.zWhy: a war said to end only by dialogue is a strait not yet opened by force

lines.quote: further escalation between Iran and the US would create nothing but losers and seriously affect hydrocarbon prices
lines.note: THE PRICE NAMED: the French minister prices the next strike into hydrocarbons — the crunch's cause stated by a foreign ministry. 'Nothing but losers' is the page's one verdict phrase
lines.zWhy: a strike priced into fuel is a strait whose closure is already in the price

lines.quote: the eight would first urge both sides to show maximum restraint; the region cannot afford another escalation
lines.note: 'cannot afford' — the frame of exhaustion; 'both sides' puts the US and Iran on one footing before the lane
lines.zWhy: both sides asked for restraint is a strait held by neither

lines.quote: the goal is de-escalation to guarantee freedom of navigation
lines.note: THE OBJECT NAMED: freedom of navigation is what the Italian minister says is not guaranteed. The Strait read as not open, in the plainest words on the page
lines.zWhy: a freedom to be guaranteed is a freedom not presently had

lines.quote: the problem cannot be solved purely militarily; dialogue must be promoted to reopen Hormuz
lines.note: 'reopen' — the lowest word on the page: a strait described as closed by a G7 foreign minister, with force named as insufficient to open it. The challenge predicate to 'under US control'
lines.zWhy: a strait to be reopened by dialogue is not open under anyone's control

lines.quote: the warnings came as the US ambassador to Türkiye, Tom Barrack, said Washington could absolutely strike Iran this weekend
lines.note: THE CLOCK — the force (slate01), marked: 'this weekend' is the earliest date any source has put on the post-election plan (NYT 10-21: after 11-03; FT via AJ 10-22: refused on timing). Two clocks on one page: the ministers' and the strike's
lines.zWhy: a strike dated to the weekend reads the Strait as a theater, not a lane

lines.quote: Trump is open and available and accessible to a deal, and has been clear about his demands
lines.note: constitutive — Washington's voice on the page (an X podcast with Mario Nawfal). The deal he offers is the holder's lever; the Strait is not in his sentence

lines.quote: any US action would not seek regime change; the aim is rebalancing so that there are no hostages and the threats end
lines.note: constitutive — the envoy's aim stated against Netanyahu's 'primary objective' of 10-22 (aj_2026-10-22_regime_change): the two principals of the next offensive name different ends on consecutive days

lines.quote: the eight-nation summit is a first-of-its-kind attempt to discuss the parameters of the regional conflicts and possible solutions
lines.note: the masthead's frame — 'first-of-its-kind' sizes the meeting, not the Strait
lines.zWhy: a first-of-its-kind meeting is called when the standing arrangement has failed

lines.quote: the participants have differing national interests, especially on the Gulf crisis; the Turkish minister stressed that what happens in the Gulf affects the wider world
lines.note: the correspondent notes the split inside the eight — the Gulf states and the Europeans do not want the same thing from the lane
lines.zWhy: eight interests on one strait is a strait no single hand holds

lines.quote: urgent need for dialogue on the US-Israel war on Iran; rejects measures restricting lawful navigation; calls for the full resumption of secure passage through Hormuz
lines.note: THE STATEMENT: 'full resumption' — passage is not secure and not full, by four governments two of which border the Gulf. The restrictor is unnamed: Iran's mines and toll, or the US blockade on Iran's oil — the ambiguity is the shadow's shape on this page
lines.zWhy: a passage to be fully resumed is a strait presently restricted
